text: A supplier reports a change: lecithin RM-114 becomes soy lecithin from lot VL-2291.
action: Supplier signs in and writes the change notice
voice: It starts the way it does today: a supplier sends a change notice.

text: The notice and its spec PDF arrive at Northfield QA as a new case.
voice: The spec PDF goes with it, and LabelLock opens a case.

text: QA sees the new notice in the inbox, with its case status.
action: QA specialist signs in; notice listed as RECEIVED
voice: Our QA specialist sees it land in the inbox.

text: Opening it brings up the case workspace.
voice: One click opens the case.

text: Run the agent. Claude reads the email and the PDF, live.
voice: She runs the agent. Claude reads the email and the PDF.

text: Each field has its exact quote and source. Anything not stated is marked MISSING.
action: Extracted fields with quotes, sources, MISSING flag
voice: Every value is backed by an exact quote, and anything the supplier didn't say is flagged, not guessed.

text: Allergen decisions come from rules. The AI only extracts, with evidence.
voice: Soy is mapped by a named rule. The AI extracts; the rules decide.

text: Oat Crunch Bar already declares soy: no impact, so the agent does nothing.
voice: Each batch is checked against its own label. Oat Crunch Bar already declares soy, so nothing happens.

text: Honey Granola Bites declares milk only: hold and relabel.
voice: Honey Granola Bites only declares milk: hold and relabel.

text: Allergy-Smart Seed Bar claims free from the top 9 allergens: claim conflict.
voice: And the Allergy-Smart bar promises free from the top nine. That claim is now false.

text: Protective holds are placed automatically, then re-read and VERIFIED.
voice: Holds go on automatically, and LabelLock reads them back to prove they took.

text: The state lives in the warehouse system itself: here FG-1041 is HELD.
voice: Not just in our database: the warehouse system itself shows the stock on hold.

text: Pulling FG-1043 off shipment L-552 is restricted: it waits for a QA manager.
voice: Taking product off a customer shipment is a bigger step, so it waits for a manager.

text: A QA specialist gets no approve button.
action: Specialist's Approvals page without approve controls
voice: Permissions are real. A specialist can't approve...

text: Called directly, the server refuses too: 403 Forbidden.
action: Direct API call page with the real 403 response
voice: ...and if she called the API directly, the server says no.

text: Releasing held stock without an approved disposition is refused by policy.
action: Shipping supervisor's release request refused: POLICY_VIOLATION
voice: Nobody can release held stock until QA records what happens to it.

text: The QA manager reviews the request and approves it with a comment.
action: Manager approves the removal on Approvals
voice: The QA manager reviews and approves.

text: LabelLock removes FG-1043, re-reads shipment L-552, and marks it VERIFIED.
voice: LabelLock pulls the batch, re-reads the shipment to confirm it's gone, and the case is contained.

text: Test: we inject a fault so the warehouse silently fails to apply holds.
action: Admin switches on the WMS fault in Settings
voice: Now a test. We make the warehouse lie: it will say holds worked when they didn't.

text: Same notice, same run.
voice: Same notice. Same run.

text: Warehouse said OK. LabelLock re-checked: still available. One safe retry, then VERIFY_FAILED.
voice: The warehouse said OK. LabelLock checked anyway, found the stock still available, retried once, and flagged the failure.

text: The case is escalated to a person. It is never marked contained.
voice: So the case goes to a person. It is never marked contained.

text: The case report: each batch's outcome and the time to containment.
voice: The report shows what happened to every batch.

text: ROI: measured results from 20 test scenarios, kept apart from editable assumptions.
action: ROI dashboard: Measured section, then Assumptions
voice: And the ROI page keeps measured results apart from assumptions you can edit.

text: Assumptions are inputs, not results. Estimates appear only once manual runs are timed.
voice: Assumptions stay inputs. No savings are claimed until real manual runs are timed.
